findings.description: The fold swaps the test stage's `pm run test` for `npx --no-install vitest run …`. A Yarn Berry Plug'n'Play repo (`"test": "vitest run"`, vitest and `@vitest/coverage-v8` declared) has no `node_modules/.bin/vitest`, so its test stage, which used to pass, now hard-fails in the gate and in init/audit/land.
findings.body:
The fold replaces the test stage's `<pm> run test` with a hardcoded `npx --no-install vitest run …` ([typescript.adapter.ts#L239-L254](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/4393901bcc00788c2759324d7366b0d5b2cd49e1/src/adapters/typescript.adapter.ts#L239-L254)). `coveredTest` checks the script's text, but it never checks that this launcher can start vitest in places where `<pm> run test` can ([#L431-L454](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/4393901bcc00788c2759324d7366b0d5b2cd49e1/src/adapters/typescript.adapter.ts#L431-L454); compare `packageManager` at [#L175-L179](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/4393901bcc00788c2759324d7366b0d5b2cd49e1/src/adapters/typescript.adapter.ts#L175-L179)).

Take a Yarn Berry Plug'n'Play repo (Plug'n'Play is Yarn's default linker) with `"test": "vitest run"` and `@vitest/coverage-v8` declared. It has no `node_modules/.bin/vitest`, so `npx --no-install` can't find the binary. Nothing in `src/` detects or refuses PnP.

Before this PR, the same npx launcher failed only inside `coverage()`. That reported coverage as "not measured", and `yarn run test` still decided the test stage. Now that failure becomes the test stage's result:
- **`pup init`, `pup audit` and `pup land`:** the stage runs in the installed main checkout ([init.service.ts#L259-L266](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/4393901bcc00788c2759324d7366b0d5b2cd49e1/src/core/init.service.ts#L259-L266)). The baseline stores test FAIL and reports that the gate will hard-fail the stage.
- **The gate** ([merge-gate.service.ts#L1240-L1253](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/4393901bcc00788c2759324d7366b0d5b2cd49e1/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L1240-L1253)): in a zero-install PnP repo where `yarn run test` used to pass, the test stage now fails on every session.

There are two possible fixes:
- Fold only when `node_modules/.bin/vitest` exists in the checkout.
- Launch the folded run through the detected package manager (`yarn vitest run …`, `pnpm exec vitest …`), so vitest starts the same way the test script starts it.

(The npx lookup behaviour comes from what we know of npm; npm's source isn't in-tree, hence medium confidence.)

findings.description: The SIGKILL grace timer is cancelled when the direct child's `'close'` fires (`settle` → `untrack` → `clearTimeout(live.killTimer)`), not when the whole group is gone. A group member that ignores or delays SIGTERM/SIGINT and doesn't hold the stdout/stderr pipes therefore outlives a timed-out, flooding or interrupted stage and is never SIGKILLed. The timeout and ENOBUFS paths close the pipes up front, so `'close'` fires as soon as the direct child exits. Such a survivor keeps writing into the checkout or scratch dir, which is the ENOTEMPTY case `removeGateDir`'s doc describes. Possible fix: in `settle`, when `failure !== undefined || live.interruptedBy`, call `signalGroup(child, 'SIGKILL')` before clearing the timer.

`measureStaticDebt` now runs alongside the test run. The TypeScript adapter's in-process `readSources` lists the checkout's source files and then reads each one, and the sandbox lets the test run write anywhere in that checkout. A suite that creates and deletes `.ts` fixtures in the repo can make the read fail with ENOENT, which rejects the whole init/gate, or put transient files into the stored dead-code/duplication baseline. Before, these capabilities ran only after the suite finished.

Duplicated Code: the 'which run gets folded coverage' choice and the 'wait for all, then rethrow any GateInterruptedError' block were added twice, in init's measureStages and the gate's measureBranch (src/core/merge-gate.service.ts:1236-1241 and 1306-1316), and the two copies already differ. Decision 72 is about init and the gate setting coverage the same way, and this is the logic that can drift between them.

Data Clumps: the same command shape `{ command; args; writablePaths? }` is written out inline in four new places in two files (merge-gate runCommand and commandStage, init runBaselineStage at src/core/init.service.ts:144, and init's `run` at :247 as `Omit<GateCommand,'stage'> & { writablePaths?: string[] }`). CoveredTestRun in src/adapters/types/adapter.types.ts:123-127 already declares command, args and writablePaths.

Duplicated Code: the new `report()` closure in `instrumentedRun` repeats the same "instrumented vitest run failed" message that `coverage()`'s catch already builds at line 425 (an unchanged context line in the diff).

Decision 84 (lines 4368-4374) still says the `withMergeLock` listener's body "never runs, since a synchronous body never yields to the event loop". Decision 95 makes that body async and moves the lock release into the gate's `finally`, but never says it refines or supersedes 84, so 84's text now contradicts the code.

`CONFIG_READ_MAX_BYTES` is a byte threshold defined in the adapter file, while general.md §No hardcoded values puts thresholds in the area's `*.constants.ts` (here `typescript-debt.constants.ts`) as a named export with a JSDoc.

`EXEC_MAX_BUFFER_BYTES` and `INTERRUPT_GRACE_MS` are new file-local numeric thresholds. general.md §No hardcoded values puts these in a `*.constants.ts`, and `merge-gate.constants.ts` already holds the neighbouring gate timeouts such as `GATE_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS`.

The new `vi.mock('node:fs', …)` and `vi.mock('./merge-gate.constants.js', …)` mock in-scope modules to force a removal failure and a short timeout. testing.md §When `vi.mock` is right reserves `vi.mock` for out-of-process concerns such as tmux or `claude -p`.

`initProject` (and `auditProject`, src/core/audit.service.ts:164-168) carry a call-site comment, "Not async, so measureBaseline's refusals still throw (see there)", that repeats `measureBaseline`'s JSDoc. AGENTS.md §Comments says to delete such call-site copies.

The opening sentences of the new `coveredTest` comment block restate `CoveredTestRun`/`coveredTest`'s JSDoc in adapter.types.ts (AGENTS.md §Comments, duplicated seam docs). Only the two-checkout and threshold reasoning is specific to this adapter.

Decision 95's "One run" paragraph says the fold checks only the trusted `test` script and the trusted root's vitest/vite config. `coveredTest` applies the script, pre/post and thresholds checks to both the trusted and the measured checkout. Say "in the trusted checkout and the measured one".

Decision 95's "Interrupts" paragraph ties the SIGKILL escalation only to forwarded signals. It omits that a timed-out or ENOBUFS-flooded stage also has its pipes closed and is SIGKILLed after the grace, as the final commit's `stop()` does.

`readSources`, `complexity` and the coverage `report()` read session-controlled paths with plain `readFileSync`. A FIFO left there by the build or the test child blocks pup's main thread while it holds the merge lock (python.adapter.ts:~378 has the same pattern). Now that these reads overlap running children, a blocked loop also stops their timeouts and interrupt forwarding. Reusing the PR's own `readPlainFile` would close this.
